hook.line: SEO is dead. The new way is answer engine optimization.
hook.visual: Close selfie in a home office with trophies behind; white title box 'SEO is [skull emoji] / How To Rank In AI', dismissive hand wave, then a closer jump cut.

beats.what: Title card 'SEO is [skull]' plus 'How To Rank In AI' under the face while he says SEO is dead
Jump cut closer and handheld as he names the replacement, answer engine optimization
Cut to the laptop screen filmed by phone: browser tab of the tool's site, step one
Zoom punch into the screen on the tool's claim to lead AI SEO
Analytics table with AI-chat referral rows ticked, as proof of 'thousands of visitors'
Tracked keyword rankings list for a client while he explains how it ranks you
Site audit results page with severity badges: on-page fixes done for you
A published blog article on screen: 'completely hands-off' writing
Backlink table with domain ratings scrolls past
Back to his face, smiling, for price, white-label resale and the comment keyword

why_it_works: 'SEO is dead' is a short provocative claim with a skull emoji, so the topic and the stance land in 1 s
Each feature claim is paired with the real dashboard screen it refers to, so the pitch looks like proof instead of an ad
The tool is named at 10 s and the rest is a feature walk-through, so viewers know exactly what they are getting
Comment-keyword CTA for the link drives shares (507) and comments without an outbound link
weaknesses: Screens are filmed off a laptop with a phone, so they are tilted, blurry and partly unreadable
Basically an affiliate ad; the 'AEO' idea itself is never explained
Middle 28 s has no face, so the personal energy of the hook drops
for_robert: Pair each claim with the actual screen it is about, but show it as a clean capture; Fred can tap or circle the one number that matters instead of a shaky phone-filmed laptop.
